ruling.recommended_action: Send to manual review: F3 (18:17–18:23, +2.98 km) is undetermined under RD-5/G13, so the refund amount cannot be fixed on this record. Reviewer to confirm whether the driven 18:17–18:23 segment lies on Lower Delta Road (F9, F10 / F12); if it is not tied to that road, refund 4.68 km × $1.4098/km = $6.60; if it is, refund 1.70 km × $1.4098/km = $2.40 (SGD, Ryde voucher per NS-7). No account flag (F18, RD-6).
ruling.reasoning:
Preliminary: this is a metered RydeTAXI trip (F8), so extra kilometres enter the fare directly and RD-2's RydeTAXI branch applies: refund = Σ(extra_km of non-exempt segments) × this trip's per-km rate (F5, F8) [RD-2]. RD-1 requires each off-route segment to be audited separately, and the trace settles that neither segment is excused by RD-4(a) — no incident on the replaced stretch (F15) — so only RD-3/RD-5 can excuse them (F3, F4) [RD-1][RD-4].

Safety screen (SAFE-1): I read the complaint, both chat messages (F9, F10) and the driver's statement (F12). The exchange is a routing negotiation — a question about going round a jam and a one-word agreement; nothing threatens, intimidates, harasses, or alleges dangerous driving, and no injury or collision is raised. Safety concern: none [SAFE-1].

F3 (18:17–18:23, +2.98 km): before 18:17 the driver asked "can I go round via Lower Delta Road?" (F9, 18:12) and the rider answered "Sure, no problem." (F10, 18:13) — a rider message sent before the segment, so RD-5 is engaged. Read in context the words are a SPECIFIC named road or area, not a general "whichever way is faster" choice, and no fact ties the driven 18:17–18:23 path to Lower Delta Road: no stop measured on that road, no message placing the car there, no road name for the driven path — timing alone does not tie them. Nothing places the segment elsewhere either (the driver's statement about GPS rerouting, F12, names no road), so the scope of the named-road agreement cannot be read off this record and the segment is undetermined under RD-5/G13; both advocates state the same ground (named_road_untied) [RD-5]. This finding changes the amount, so per NS-7 the case goes to a person rather than being executed here.

F4 (18:26–18:31, +1.70 km): the chat record is complete and every message timestamped (F11), and the only rider message in it is the 18:13 "Sure, no problem." (F10) — nothing the rider wrote precedes the 18:26 turn-off. The driver's statement that the second turn-off was his GPS rerouting (F12) is his post-trip account, not rider consent (G11), and an agreement to travel via Lower Delta Road cannot cover a later turn-off elsewhere (RD-5). Both advocates state the same ground (consent_after_or_none), so this segment counts and its 1.70 km is refundable [RD-5][RD-2].

Amount: the trace's rate is the trip's distance fare ÷ distance km = $27.52 ÷ 19.52 km = $1.4098/km (F5, F8); the rate is never rounded. Because F3 is undetermined and it changes the amount, the refund is either 4.68 km (F3+F4) × $1.4098 = $6.5978 → $6.60, or, if F3 is tied to the agreed road, 1.70 km (F4) × $1.4098 = $2.3967 → $2.40 [F3][F4][F5][F8][RD-2]. The $7.46 billed excess line covers 5.29 km (F5) against the 4.68 km the two segments add, and RD-2 leaves that ~0.61 km corridor/rounding residue unrefunded; the $0.11 metered waiting unit stays with the meter (F6) [RD-2][RD-3]. Since the amount is undeterminable on this record, I do not enter an amount and the outcome is escalate.

Account action: RD-6 needs route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1; the driver's profile shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days (F18), so no flag_account and the trace's ✗ stands [RD-6]. F1's +5.3 km overall is background only — RD-2 refunds per segment, not the total against the optimal route [F1][RD-2].

segment_findings.reason: Rider message F10 (18:13) precedes the segment start 18:17 and answers the driver's naming of Lower Delta Road (F9, 18:12), but no fact ties this driven segment to that road — no stop on it, no locating message, no road-name fact for the driven path — and nothing places it elsewhere either, so under RD-5 and G13 the scope of the named-road agreement is not settled on this record. Both advocates read it the same way. The finding changes the amount, so the case goes to manual review; the segment is neither exempted nor executed as refundable here.

The complete, fully timestamped chat record (F11) contains no rider message after 18:13 (F10), so no rider agreement precedes the 18:26 start of this segment; the driver's statement that it was his GPS rerouting (F12) is a post-trip claim, not rider consent (G11), and the earlier agreement to Lower Delta Road cannot cover a later turn-off elsewhere. No RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 exemption applies, so its 1.70 km extra is refundable under RD-2 if F3 is resolved in the driver's favour.

rejected_claims.reason: Rejected as far as it claims a full exemption for F3: the rider's F10 'Sure, no problem.' answers a question naming Lower Delta Road (F9), and RD-5 requires a record tying the driven segment to that road; nothing in F3, F9, F10 or F11 does so, while F12 names no road either, so the segment is undetermined rather than exempt (RD-5, G13). The driver's own brief concedes it is at best named_road_untied.

Rejected: RD-4 needs a qualifying traffic incident on the replaced stretch, and F15 records none; speed bands 4 and 5 (F13, F14) are neither band 1 nor 2 and are corroborative only, not a standalone exemption, and F16 shows fair weather (RD-4).

Rejected: RD-2 refunds per unexempted segment at the trip's per-km rate; the billed $7.46 line (F5) does not cap the per-segment calculation, and its ~0.61 km residue over the 4.68 km of F3+F4 is simply not refunded (F3, F4, F5; RD-2).

Rejected as unnecessary: flag_account under RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1, and F18 shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days; the profile also cannot shield the unexempted segment (RD-6, RD-1).

Accepted only as the reading that leaves F3 undetermined: the named-road agreement (F9, F10) is untied to the driven segment, so it neither exempts nor refunds it (RD-5, G13); that is why the case goes to a person and no amount executes here.

Accepted as to the absence of any RD-4 exemption (F15, F16), but it does not by itself dispose of F3: the RD-4 screen is settled by the trace, while F3 turns on the scope of the rider's named-road agreement under RD-5.

Not executable as stated: it refunds 4.68 km (F3 + F4) at $1.4098/km, but F3 is undetermined on this record, so the $6.60 figure is one of two possible amounts a reviewer must choose between, not a computable award here (F3, F4, F5, F8; RD-2, RD-5, NS-7).
